name: Ulli Theeyal
subtitle: dark roasted-coconut and shallot curry, sour with tamarind

ingredients.note: small ones; halve any larger than a walnut

ingredients.qty: 1 cup grated, fresh or thawed frozen
ingredients.note: the whole dish depends on roasting this properly
more than this turns the gravy bitter

ingredients.qty: lime-sized ball, soaked in 200ml warm water

prepNotes: Soak the tamarind in 200ml warm water for 20 minutes, then squeeze and strain; discard the fibres.
Peel the shallots ahead — 300g takes a good 15 minutes and this is the slow part of the recipe.
Have the ground spices measured into one bowl before you start roasting the coconut; it goes from brown to burnt in seconds.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the coconut oil in a heavy pan and roast the grated coconut over medium-low heat, stirring almost constantly, for 12-15 minutes until it is a deep even brown and smells nutty.
steps.tip: Do not walk away. The coconut sits pale for eight minutes and then colours all at once.

steps.text: Add the fenugreek seeds and roast 30 seconds more, then take the pan off the heat.
Stir the coriander powder, kashmiri chilli, chilli powder and turmeric into the hot coconut off the heat and let the residual warmth cook them for 1 minute.
Cool completely, then grind with 150ml water to a very smooth, dark paste — a full 3-4 minutes in the blender.
steps.tip: Any grit left in the paste stays grit in the finished curry. Grind longer than you think you need to.

steps.text: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp coconut oil in the same pan and fry the whole shallots over medium heat for 8 minutes until browned at the edges and softened.
Pour in the strained tamarind water and 350ml water, add the salt, and simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the shallots are tender to a knife tip.
Stir in the ground coconut paste, rinse the blender with a splash of water and add that too.
Simmer gently 12-15 minutes, uncovered, until the gravy darkens and thickens enough to coat a spoon and oil beads at the surface.
steps.tip: The oil separating at the edges is the sign it is done. Rushing this leaves a raw, chalky taste.

steps.text: Stir in the jaggery and cracked pepper, taste, and correct salt and sourness.
In a small pan heat a teaspoon of coconut oil, crackle the mustard seeds, add the dried chillies and curry leaves, and pour the tempering over the curry.
steps.tip: Cover the pan for a second as the curry leaves go in — they spit hard.

steps.text: Rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with rice.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated and genuinely improves on the second day. Reheat gently on the stovetop with a splash of water; do not boil hard or the coconut paste splits.
